summary: Iter-33 verified the four items requested: (1) Site Mode builder now renders cleanly for admin — no React hook-order crash, canvas, pages bar, block templates, outline, style panel, AI editor and every toolbar button (Preview, Generate site with AI, Lock all, History, Import from URL, Try another look, Upload logo, Save) all mount and are interactive. (2) NEW 'Lock all / Unlock all' button (data-testid=lock-all-pages-btn) toggles: initial label 'Lock all' → click → toast 'Locked all 4 page(s) + Overview content' → label flips to 'Unlock all', page tabs get an amber padlock, and Overview → Content lock reflects 'Content locked'. Unlock path prompts confirm() and flips back. (3) NEW landing page 'Editing on / Editing off' toggle (data-testid=landing-edit-mode-toggle): renders only for admin, initial label 'Editing on · click to browse', clicks flip to 'Editing off · click to edit', label PERSISTS across a full reload (backed by localStorage os_landing_edit), and non-admin (logged-out) visitors do NOT see the toggle. When editing off, hero/nav CTAs navigate normally (onClick={admin?undefined:go}). (4) Version compare — clicking Compare in History opens the diff dialog: shows sections back / dropped / changed counts, inline word-level diff (strikethrough removed / green added) per field, and a working Restore this version button. Backend: 11/11 pytest pass in 17s (test_iter33_lock_all_edit_requests.py). Covered POST /apps/{id}/pages/lock-all owner-happy path (200, {locked, pages, content_locked}, pages.locked=true for all rows, apps.content_locked=true), route-order sanity (lock-all is NOT swallowed by the /pages/{page_id}/lock route registered on the same prefix — FastAPI matches on the trailing segment), editor 403, owner can PATCH a page while all locked, editor gets 423 with detail containing 'locked' / 'request', full edit-request round trip (editor POST edit-request → admin POST inbox approve → editor GET edit-access returns can_edit=true+grant → editor PATCH succeeds → next PATCH gets 423 because the grant is single-use and was consumed), version diff endpoint returns {summary:{added,removed,edited,sections_now,sections_after,identical}, changes:[…]}, POST /site/import-zip returns 423 when content lock is on (mode=replace) and 200+job_id when unlocked. Frontend smoke observed: History dialog shows dated entries with LATEST chip, per-page Compare & restore buttons AND a top 'Undo a whole site change · Put this site back' section for the batch snapshots flagged in iter-32 — that gap is now closed in the UI. No 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay anywhere. Route conflict check (asked in the request): POST /apps/{app_id}/pages/{page_id} does NOT exist as a route — only PATCH/DELETE do — so POST /apps/{app_id}/pages/lock-all cannot be swallowed by a page-id path (verified live: it returns the correct JSON, not 405/404). GET /apps/{app_id}/pages/{page_id}/... routes require a trailing segment, so 'lock-all' likewise cannot collide.

minor.issue: Body accepts {locked:bool} but there's no top-level assert_unlocked check when locking. That is by design (locking is safe), but the endpoint could still fail if a page doc has no locked field yet — currently harmless because $set writes the field. Non-blocking.

When an edit request is approved and email fails to send the caller still gets 200 (logged.exception + swallow). Fine, but consider surfacing 'email_sent':false in the response so the UI can hint 'we couldn't email the client'.

issues: The toolbar row wraps to 2 lines at 1920×1080 when Lock-all is added because there are now 9 buttons + logo upload. Not a bug, but worth grouping (e.g. move Import from URL / Try another look / Upload logo into an ellipsis-menu) to keep the row on one line.

critical_code_review_comments: page_guard.lock_all_pages writes {locked, locked_at} to every page AND sets content_locked at the tenant, but does NOT snapshot the current pages before locking. That is intentional (locking is non-destructive), but if the app ever grows a 'lock also snapshots so we can revert to now-locked state' feature the write order matters.

edit_requests.consume_grant is exported from register() but is only actually called from studio.update_page — verified. If a new save/restore path is added it must call consume_grant, otherwise a single approval becomes multi-use. Consider centralising the 'save with grant' pattern in a helper.

Builder.jsx access/refreshAccess hooks are now correctly declared BEFORE any useEffect that reads them (fix confirmed). BUT toggleAllLocks does `setPages(pages.map(...))` off the stale closure — if the user clicks Lock-all right after a page create/delete this could drop the just-added page from local state. Use setPages(p => p.map(...)) for safety.

Landing.jsx uses `localStorage.getItem('os_landing_edit') !== '0'` as the initial value — so editing is ON by default for admins. That is what the spec asks, but it means the very first admin visit auto-hijacks the CTAs (hero button and pricing CTAs become non-navigating). Consider defaulting to OFF the first time so admins have to opt into edit mode explicitly.

zip_import.build_from_zip decodes CSS with `[:300_000]` per file and joins to `[:900_000]` — for a well-designed site that is plenty, but a single massive tailwind.css can blow past 300 KB and be silently truncated. Non-blocking.

success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke — Site Mode renders, Lock-all toggle works with correct toast + amber padlocks + Overview sync, Landing edit-mode toggle flips label + persists across reload + hidden for logged-out, History → Compare opens diff dialog with per-field inline word diff and working Restore

rca of the issue: No new bug found. The hook-order crash reported at session start is fixed (access/setAccess/refreshAccess declared before the useEffect that reads them at lines 78-83) and Site Mode now renders end-to-end. Route conflict risk asked about in the request does NOT materialise: FastAPI only registers POST for /apps/{app_id}/pages (create) and /apps/{app_id}/pages/{page_id}/lock (single-page lock) — there is no POST /apps/{app_id}/pages/{page_id}, so POST /apps/{app_id}/pages/lock-all resolves to lock_all_pages() as expected (verified by 200 response with the {locked, pages, content_locked} shape defined in page_guard.py:100).
